notes: Base attribution pass at f08ee42 probed 12 mutants over the pre-existing behaviours that are single-edit mutatable; 12/12 KILLED, every one by a test already on main, baseline green at 27. No pre-existing gap was found, so the tests this run added are additive rather than covering for main.

Branch pass at e26ede4 probed 18 mutants over the behaviours this run introduced; 18/18 KILLED, baseline green at 54. Those kills credit this run's own tests, because the behaviours did not exist at base.

The third candidate is absent from 'filed' because it was fixed in the same PR rather than left open: BindingTooFresh reported an age of zero for a binding stamped ahead of the clock, collapsing 'wait and retry' together with 'this chain's clock went backwards'. Split into BindingStampedInFuture. The adversarial pass found it, and a test written earlier in the run had PINNED it, which is the failure mode the skill opens with.

Process defects in this run, recorded rather than hidden: the branch pass was first run after this run's own tests were written, forfeiting attribution and requiring the base pass above as recovery; the adversarial pass was skipped on the first attempt; and the first pass ran sequentially on one checkout instead of fanning out. The base pass was then run 12-way across 12 fresh clones at 193s, against 944s for 18 sequential mutants.

Snapshot regeneration must run INSIDE the probe suite command. Mutating AddressRegistry moves its bytecode, so a stale pin makes testDeployMatchesPins and every LibAddressRegistry code-hash guard fail for every mutant regardless of behaviour, which is a universal killer that hides which test discriminates. The first attempt attributed all ten mutants to testDeployMatchesPins and was discarded.
